# [FR]: Make ctrl+tab better

- State: closed
- Author: ry430
- Created: 2026-03-19T18:26:43Z
- Updated: 2026-04-19T10:45:35Z
- Repository: imputnet/helium
- Number: #1122

## Labels

- feat

---

### Description

Add an ui interface for ctrl tab menu. and add an option to use Alt+q and Alt+w to go back and forward between tabs.

### Who's implementing?

- [ ] I'm willing to implement this feature myself

### The problem

The Ctrl+Tab on Helium is not good compared to Vivaldi or Firefox.
No interface to indicate which tab you are going to switch to after you do Ctrl+Tab, and no options to switch between recently used tabs.
As a person who uses lots of shortcuts for tab switching, this is a problem, and a lot of people who are used to Firefox or Vivaldi as well.

### Possible solutions

There is a good extension called Tab Flick.
Unfortunently this extension barely works and have alot of bugs. I suspect of chromes aggressive battery saving, and it takes time to boot up an extension. I think it will be a good productivity improvement in terms of time and usability if this feature were built into the browser. Thank you.

https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/tab-flick-%E2%9C%A8-%E2%80%94-switch-your/kdddoanokjocdkbkmgnkkcemjepknlgm

 

Here is a Vivaldi tab cycler too.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6eb0e536-ecf7-45fa-b26c-9d88a7ab5f6f)

# [FR]: Show tab preview on tab switch

- State: open
- Author: zeroaddresss
- Created: 2025-10-10T10:22:42Z
- Updated: 2026-04-19T13:46:34Z
- Repository: imputnet/helium
- Number: #238

## Labels

- feat
- approved

---

### Description

When switching tabs with <C+Tab>, add tab preview

### Who's implementing?

- [ ] I'm willing to implement this feature myself

### The problem

Feature request: add a tab preview feature, similar to Windows' +Tab, for faster and more visual tab switching.
Instead of directly switching tabs with Ctrl/Cmd+Tab, show a preview overlay of open tabs. This allows users to quickly select the desired tab using keyboard or mouse.
Benefits:
• Faster tab navigation, especially with many tabs.
• Improved visual identification of tab content.

See attached screen recording for a demonstration of the expected UI behavior: https://streamable.com/ktjc8e

urls.content:
# [FR]: Ability to enable tab switching using MRU order like MacOS Command+Tab

- State: closed
- Author: jschol3s
- Created: 2025-09-26T04:49:42Z
- Updated: 2025-12-28T11:13:36Z
- Repository: imputnet/helium
- Number: #111

## Labels

- feat
- approved

---

### Description

Add a feature that enables tab switching (Ctrl+Tab) that cycles through most recently used tabs, instead of cycling in visual order.

### Who's implementing?

- [ ] I'm willing to implement this feature myself

### The problem

Currently, Ctrl+Tab cycles through tabs in their visual order. This makes it harder to switch quickly between the tabs I'm actively working on. This was my favorite feature of Arc, and I would love to have it in Helium. 

### Possible solutions

Make Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab switch between tabs in MRU order, similar to the macOS Command+Tab app switcher. Ideally, repeated presses should cycle through tabs in order of last activation.

### Additional context

This is a common feature in IDEs and browsers like Firefox and Arc. It improves productivity for users who keep many tabs open, and comes naturally to most devs. In firefox, they just have a checkbox in settings with this as the description: Ctrl+Tab cycles through tabs in recently used order

- State: closed

- Repository: imputnet/helium
- Number: #1101

## Labels

- feat

---

### Description

Add alt-tab style switching for recent tabs

### Who's implementing?

- [ ] I'm willing to implement this feature myself

### The problem

It would be a massive UX improvement to have an alt-tab behavior for switching between tabs based on most recently used (MRU) order, just like OS window switching. Juggling multiple specific tabs would be way faster and it would make the overall browsing experience a lot smoother.

### Possible solutions

add a shortcut like ctrl+tab to cycle through recent tabs in MRU order
